• **HSV**: hue ≈ 270° (or 300° depending on convention), high saturation, medium value.
• **Lab**: a negative a‑value (blue‑red axis) and a positive b‑value (yellow‑blue axis). | Color‑based segmentation, feature extraction, or marker detection. | | **Detection** | Thresholding in HSV or Lab is common because hue is less affected by lighting changes. | Isolate purple objects (e.g., purple flowers, traffic signs, or colored markers). | | **Marker/Tracking** | Purple is relatively uncommon in natural scenes, so it’s often chosen as a marker color for tracking algorithms (e.g., in robotics or AR). | Color‑coded fiducial markers, object tracking, or pose estimation. | | **Segmentation** | In semantic segmentation datasets, a class may be labeled with a purple color for visualization. | Visualizing segmentation masks or labeling classes in training data. | | **Augmented Reality** | Purple tags or stickers can be used to anchor virtual objects. | Marker‑based AR, pose estimation. | So, in computer vision, purple is just another color that can be encoded in a color space, thresholded, segmented, or used as a distinctive marker for detection and tracking tasks.
